value.rationale: For a natural family of high-dimensional canonical Euclidean simplices, a single hub carries half of the random-exposure mass even as its fraction of vertices tends to zero. The first nonzero correction sharply detects forming pairwise triangles while keeping the same graph order and hub degree: a \(\sqrt5\) amplification. This is a motivated geometric edge-sensitivity law, not a finite-table recomputation or arbitrary slice; it meaningfully refines an existing asymptotic.
